Get transparency data for a briefing.

Shows how the briefing was made: model, sources, articles,
phase 1 analysis, and processing stats.

Viewable by the owner and — for public briefings (public topic) — by any
logged-in reader. The `view` permission resolves to `is_public or owner`.

OWNER-ONLY INVARIANT: `_resolve_memory_source` leaks the internal memory
source id + forge_feed_id, and A/B variant data exposes raw prompt
filenames + LLM outputs. Both are gated on `is_owner` inside
`_build_transparency_response`, so non-owners viewing a public briefing
never receive them. See HEA-305 / HEA-504.
Expose the LB feature flags so the frontend can conditionally render UI.

List the authenticated user's past Link Bankruptcy briefings.

Scoped history surface (HEA-369) — LB briefings are hidden from the
regular dashboard (their backing goal carries ``purpose=
'link_bankruptcy'``, which ``get_by_user`` filters out), so without
this a user who loses the direct briefing URL has no way back to a
past submission. Returns rows newest-first, including ones whose
ephemeral-goal cleanup (HEA-334) has already run.

Errors:
  - 403 if the LB feature flag is disabled

Per-URL disposition for one LB briefing — the accounting half of the pile.

The briefing curates; the UI accounts. A mode may feature only a subset of
the submitted URLs, so this lists every one of them and what became of it.

Everything is derived from ``briefing_submitted_urls``, never from
``sources``: LB cleanup HARD-deletes sources, so anything reconstructed
from them would vanish minutes after the briefing completes.

``featured`` is decided by canonicalized citation-matching of the briefing
summary against each row's ``entry_urls`` ∪ ``normalized``. Both sides are
canonicalized, and matching is segment-wise sub-path aware, because Forge
routinely emits ``example.com/blog/a`` for a submitted ``example.com/blog``
— matching the submitted URL alone under-reports coverage. This is
markdown string-matching of the HEA-658 fragility class: accepted for now,
structured citations are the durable fix.

post.description:
Submit a pile of URLs + topic, get one ephemeral briefing.

Returns 201 with ``{goal_id, briefing_id, status, extraction_errors}``
immediately after backing-row creation. Forge feed provisioning +
briefing generation run as a BackgroundTask via
``LinkBankruptcyService.provision_and_generate``; the user is
redirected to the IN_PROGRESS briefing viewer and polling takes
over. ``extraction_errors`` is always ``[]`` in this response —
the populated list lives on ``briefing.stats.extraction_errors``
once the BackgroundTask runs.

Errors:
  - 403 if the LB feature flag is disabled
  - 403 ANON_LB_LIMIT_REACHED if an unclaimed anonymous account has
    already used its single free submission (detail carries claim_url)
  - 429 if the user is over their daily cap (paid: shared
    manual-briefing cap; free: LB-specific LB_FREE_DAILY_CAP)
  - 400 for input validation that slipped past Pydantic
    (e.g. dedup-to-zero)

post.description:
Mint a follow-up from a briefing's What-to-do item (HEA-452 Phase 1).

Pro-gated. Idempotent on ``srv:<briefing_id>:<item_ref>`` so re-tapping
"Follow up" returns the same row instead of duplicating. The client maps
the what_to_do item's hints into the card (no server LLM — D1); we
validate ownership via the briefing and store it under ``kind='follow-up'``.

delete.description:
Delete one of the caller's follow-ups (HEA-452). Restricted to
``kind='follow-up'`` rows so it can never remove a skill-synced agent
experiment. 404 if it isn't the caller's follow-up.

patch.description:
Conclude a follow-up (verdict + optional note) or reopen it
(``status="active"``). Conclude sets the status column to ``concluded`` and
stores the verdict in ``result``; reopen clears it. Follow-up-only +
ownership-checked. Both branches write through
``ExperimentRepository.transition_with_event`` (PR #43 fix-wave F7) — a
transactional compare-and-set status write + event append in one
round-trip; response shape is unchanged from before that refactor.

post.description:
Mint a captured insight from a briefing selection (D4).

Idempotent INSERT ... DO NOTHING keyed on ``ins:<briefing_id>:<sel_hash>``
(PR #43 fix-wave F1) — re-capturing the same selection returns the
UNCHANGED existing row (200) instead of duplicating. Unlike the old
upsert()-based DO UPDATE, a re-tap after the row has moved past
'captured' (upgraded/started/concluded) is a pure read: it can never
clobber lifecycle state back to 'captured'. Authz mirrors
``create_follow_up``: you can capture from any briefing you can view.

captured -> defined (D16): attach hypothesis/criterion/horizon.

Pro-gated (``require_can_define_experiment``); the gate runs BEFORE the
row read so a free-tier caller never leaks whether the id exists.

defined -> running (or concluded -> running, the reopen-via-start path).

Order matters (spec D13/D23): the horizon-present check (422) runs BEFORE
the running-cap check (429), and neither writes anything on failure. The
running-cap is enforced twice (PR #43 fix-wave F4/F7): a soft pre-check
here (kept for the ``running_count_after`` metric and its existing
contract) and the authoritative, race-safe ``enforce_running_cap`` inside
``transition_with_event``'s own transaction.

running (or verdict_pending) -> concluded, with a user-confirmed
verdict. Any kind.

verdict_pending -> running with an extended horizon (spec §3.2, D26).

The "not yet" answer to a drafted verdict. Deliberately stricter than
``validate_transition`` alone: that table also admits ``concluded ->
running`` (reopen, which /start owns) and ``defined -> running`` (start),
so gating on the table would make this a third door onto ``running`` with
different semantics. Only a drafted verdict can be rejected.

Re-entering ``running`` consumes the per-account cap (D23), and the
rejected draft is cleared from ``result`` — it survives in the event
trail, which is where §3.4 says verdict history lives.

Any non-archived state -> archived. Archived is terminal (D24);
archiving an already-archived row is a 409.

PR #43 fix-wave F6: unlike the other four write-surface endpoints, this
one does NOT run ``validate_transition`` — agent-synced rows can carry
NULL or free-text statuses (never translated through
``adapt_legacy_status``) that aren't in the unified transition table at
all, and archiving must still work for them. The only guard is the
current status itself: 'archived' (terminal) stays a 409, everything
else may archive.

delete.description:
Hard-delete a captured insight (D24: the delete door for rows whose only
other exit is terminal archive).

Insight-only by design (1D S6). Follow-ups keep their dedicated
``DELETE /experiments/follow-ups/{id}``; agent-synced rows keep archive as
the terminal exit, because a skill re-sync would just recreate a deleted
row under the same ``client_key`` and the delete would read as a silent
no-op. Widening this to every kind is a separate decision nobody has made.

Events cascade via the FK (migration 045), so no explicit event cleanup.

ExperimentCaptureRequest.title: ExperimentCaptureRequest
ExperimentCaptureRequest.description:
POST /api/v2/experiments/capture — mint a captured insight (D4).

``origin`` is a closed set (1C R6), same reasoning as
``ExperimentUpgradeRequest.horizon``: it was free text, so a typo landed
in the ``origin`` column and quietly mis-attributed the insight's
provenance forever (a 1A deferred item). ``agent-sync`` is deliberately
NOT offered — that value belongs to the sync route, which sets it
server-side; a capture claiming it would forge provenance.

ExperimentRejectRequest.title: ExperimentRejectRequest
ExperimentRejectRequest.description:
``POST /api/v2/experiments/{id}/reject`` — verdict_pending -> running
with an extended horizon (spec §3.2, D26).

Rejecting a drafted verdict says "keep going", so the experiment needs a
new deadline. ``horizon`` omitted means "the same length again" (D26),
read from the row's ``definition.horizon``; an explicit token overrides
it. Strict (``extra="forbid"``) like the routing PATCH — this is a new
v2-only surface with no legacy client to stay compatible with.

ExperimentResponse.title: ExperimentResponse
ExperimentResponse.description: One experiment as returned by the read endpoints (UI-facing).

ExperimentRoutingRequest.title: ExperimentRoutingRequest
ExperimentRoutingRequest.description:
``PATCH /api/v2/experiments/{id}/routing`` — update delivery-routing
prefs (spec §3.7, plan Q1): briefing-email-section inclusion, reminder
cadence, mute. Strict (``extra="forbid"``) — routing is a small, closed
vocabulary, so an unrecognized key is a client bug worth surfacing, not
silently ignoring (unlike the lenient agent-sync body above).

All three fields default to ``None`` and the route builds its update dict
via ``body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`` — Pydantic's ``exclude_unset``
distinguishes "omitted" from "explicit null", which is exactly the
partial-PATCH semantics needed: an explicit ``"reminder_cadence": null``
clears the cadence, while omitting the key leaves the stored value alone.

ExperimentUpgradeRequest.title: ExperimentUpgradeRequest
ExperimentUpgradeRequest.description:
POST /api/v2/experiments/{id}/upgrade — captured -> defined (D16 gate).

``horizon`` is a closed token set (PR #43 fix-wave F8) — this is the
NEW write surface, so an invalid token 422s here rather than silently
falling back to the 30d default deep in the check-in read path. The
legacy ``FollowUpCreateRequest.horizon`` stays a lenient ``str`` — it is
the published-skill/UI contract and must not gain this restriction.

LBBriefingSectionDescriptor.title: LBBriefingSectionDescriptor
LBBriefingSectionDescriptor.description:
One section in an LB custom layout.

Deliberately not the goals API's ``BriefingSection``: that model has no
``title``/``instructions``, so free-form sections would be silently
stripped. Field-level rules live in
``synthesis_engine.core.briefing_sections.validate_briefing_sections``,
which this schema delegates to — one source of truth for both the API
boundary and the service layer.

LinkBankruptcyBriefingSummary.title: LinkBankruptcyBriefingSummary
LinkBankruptcyBriefingSummary.description:
One row in the LB history surface (``GET /link-bankruptcy/briefings``).

``topic_name`` is the backing goal's name, joined so the user has a
label to scan against. ``url_count`` is the de-duplicated count of
submitted URLs, stashed in ``briefing.stats`` at provision time so it
survives the ephemeral-goal cleanup hook (HEA-334), which soft-deletes
the ``V2Source`` rows a join would otherwise need. Both are
``Optional`` because pre-existing rows (created before this field
landed) carry neither.

``mode`` is the layout the user picked at submit time, read from the
same stats blob for the same reason. It **replaced** a ``format`` field
(HEA-651c) rather than joining it: `format` shipped 2026-08-01 behind
``LB_BRIEFING_FORMATS`` and its only readers were this repo's own
frontend and tests — the Chrome extension calls this endpoint but its
``LbBriefingSummary`` never declared the field, so nothing un-hot-fixable
depended on it. Keeping both would have put two names for one concept on
the wire, and worse, PR #42's ``link_triage`` is design-*cluster*, so a
surviving format vocabulary would render two different modes as "Triage"
the moment ``triage`` becomes reachable.

Resolution (incl. the legacy ``stats.lb_format`` bridge) is owned by
``lb_modes.mode_from_stats``; ``None`` means no layout was applied.

LinkBankruptcyConfigResponse.title: LinkBankruptcyConfigResponse
LinkBankruptcyConfigResponse.description:
Feature-flag exposure used by the frontend to gate the LB UI.

``formats_available`` is **always True** since the LB_BRIEFING_FORMATS kill
switch was retired; it once reflected that switch, and a false value told
the client to hide the picker because the backend would ignore any
``format``/``mode``/``sections`` it sent.

**Keep emitting it anyway.** Extensions at v0.2.0 read
``config.formats_available === true`` and omit ``format`` when it is falsy.
Dropping the field does not error — it silently hides the picker for every
one of those users, and installed copies cannot be hot-fixed. v0.2.1 and
later derive availability from ``modes_available`` and no longer read this
field at all, so it goes once the v0.2.0 installs are gone.

That is a question to *ask*, not to measure. A PostHog capture of the
``X-Header-Client-Version`` header briefly lived on this endpoint and was
removed: v0.2.0 sends no such header, so the event could only ever prove
v0.2.1+ was present, never that v0.2.0 was absent, and nothing recorded
total request volume to serve as a denominator. With an install base of a
handful, confirming directly beats instrumenting. The header itself is still
sent and allow-listed in CORS — it costs nothing and is worth having if the
install base ever grows enough to need a real signal.

``modes_available`` is the mode-vocabulary successor. It lists only modes
reachable today — membership in ``AVAILABLE_LB_MODES`` both unlocks a mode
(checked in ``_resolve_mode``, so every ``precreate`` caller is covered) and
publishes it here, so a mode held back pending its eval never reaches a
picker. All four are reachable as of HEA-651b (triage's gate passed
2026-08-21); the mechanism remains the way to hold a future mode back.

LinkBankruptcyDispositionResponse.title: LinkBankruptcyDispositionResponse
LinkBankruptcyDispositionResponse.description:
Response shape for ``GET /api/v2/link-bankruptcy/briefings/{id}``.

The briefing curates; the UI accounts. A mode may feature only a subset of
the pile, so this endpoint exists to show every submitted URL and what
became of it — including the ones the briefing never mentions.

Computed at read time from ``briefing_submitted_urls`` alone, so it still
works after LB cleanup has hard-deleted the sources.

error_detail.title: Error Detail
error_detail.description: Forge's structured error code (detail.error_code), if available

LinkBankruptcyExtractionError.title: LinkBankruptcyExtractionError
LinkBankruptcyExtractionError.description:
Per-URL failure surfaced in the submit response.

``stage`` is one of ``"create" | "approve" | "poll" | "approve_or_poll"``
corresponding to where the failure landed in the Forge orchestration.
``error_code`` is the HTTP status (string) or a synthesized code like
``no_pending_version``. ``error_detail`` is Forge's structured
``FeedForgeErrorCode`` (e.g. ``extractor_unavailable``,
``content_unavailable``) when present — ``None`` otherwise.

LinkBankruptcyHistoryResponse.title: LinkBankruptcyHistoryResponse
LinkBankruptcyHistoryResponse.description:
Response shape for ``GET /api/v2/link-bankruptcy/briefings``.

``total`` is the unpaginated count so the frontend can render
pagination controls against the ``limit``/``offset`` window.

LinkBankruptcySubmitRequest.title: LinkBankruptcySubmitRequest
LinkBankruptcySubmitRequest.description:
Submission payload for ``POST /api/v2/link-bankruptcy``.

Validates URL count + shape at the boundary so the service layer never
sees malformed input. ``urls`` is constrained to 1..LB_MAX_URLS (=100);
chunking into ≤25-URL Forge batches is a service-layer concern.

``format`` picks the briefing layout. ``sections`` is required when — and
accepted only when — ``format='custom'``; sending it alongside a preset
format is rejected rather than ignored, so a client that thinks it is
customizing the layout never gets a silent preset.

**Re-kick (HEA-664).** Supplying ``from_briefing_id`` instead of ``urls``
replays a past pile: the server reads that briefing's persisted
``briefing_submitted_urls`` rows and reuses them. Exactly one of the two
must be given.

The loosening of ``urls`` from required to defaulted is deliberately
*additive*: a request with neither still 422s, so no existing client
changes behavior. That matters because the published Chrome extension
(v0.2.0, `extension/src/api.ts`) calls this endpoint and always sends a
non-empty ``urls`` with no ``from_briefing_id`` — installed copies cannot
be hot-fixed, so the old shape has to keep working exactly as before.

**Scheme repair (HEA-883).** ``urls`` entries arrive from copy/paste as
often as from an address bar, so a missing scheme is normal input rather
than an error. A ``mode="before"`` validator runs ``ensure_url_scheme``
over the list, turning ``www.example.com/a`` into ``https://www.example.com/a``
before ``HttpUrl`` sees it. The declared type stays ``List[HttpUrl]`` so
everything downstream still gets a real URL, and anything that parses today
parses identically — nothing for the published extension or skill to adapt
to. Entries with no dotted host still 422, by design.

``topic_name``/``topic_description`` are likewise optional ONLY on the
re-kick path, where omitting them inherits the source briefing's goal
framing. That inheritance is the point: ``framing_hash`` is part of the
curated cache key, so a re-kick that retypes the framing even slightly
misses every URL. Letting the server copy it is what makes "identical
re-kick is near-free" actually hold.

LinkBankruptcySubmitResponse.title: LinkBankruptcySubmitResponse
LinkBankruptcySubmitResponse.description:
Response shape for ``POST /api/v2/link-bankruptcy``.

``extraction_errors`` is always ``[]`` here — the route returns
before any Forge work runs. The populated list is written to
``briefing.stats.extraction_errors`` by the BackgroundTask once
Forge provisioning completes; clients should read it from the
briefing detail endpoint, not from this response.

LinkBankruptcyUrlDisposition.title: LinkBankruptcyUrlDisposition
LinkBankruptcyUrlDisposition.description:
One submitted URL's fate in a completed LB briefing.

**Attributes are orthogonal, not a one-of-four state** (design review P1,
2026-08-06). A featured URL can also be truncated, and a single exclusive
state would hide the truncation — which violates the never-silent rule the
coverage contract is built on. The UI renders multiple badges.

url.title: Url
url.description: Portal URL to redirect user to

PreprocessingUsage.title: PreprocessingUsage
PreprocessingUsage.description:
Token spend of the per-article preprocessing calls behind this briefing.

One LLM call per raw candidate, so ``calls`` matches the funnel's
``total_fetched``. ``rejected_input_share_pct`` is the share of input tokens
spent on candidates that returned the no-relevant-content marker;
``retention_pct`` is relevant output tokens over relevant input tokens —
how much of the relevant raw text survives into Phase 1.
``calls_without_usage`` > 0 means older rows had no per-call token record
and the sums are a lower bound.

RecommendationCard.title: RecommendationCard
RecommendationCard.description: One verified candidate surfaced to the user.

RecommendationSignals.title: RecommendationSignals
RecommendationSignals.description: Trust signals rendered on each recommendation card.

min_supported.title: Min Supported
min_supported.description: Oldest skill version this API still supports (semver).

SkillVersionResponse.title: SkillVersionResponse
SkillVersionResponse.description:
Version metadata the header-briefing skill polls to decide when to upgrade.

Only `latest` is required. The optional fields are dropped from the
response when null (the route sets `response_model_exclude_none=True`), so
a maintainer can null any of them out without changing the contract.

TransparencyMemorySource.title: TransparencyMemorySource
TransparencyMemorySource.description: Owner-visible pointer to the forge-backed memory source used for a briefing.

UpdateApiKeyRequest.title: UpdateApiKeyRequest
UpdateApiKeyRequest.description:
``PATCH /api/v2/api-keys/{key_id}`` — toggle a key's experiment-start
approval setting.

status.title: Status
status.description: Subscription status: free, active, past_due, canceled

cancel_at_period_end.title: Cancel At Period End
cancel_at_period_end.description: Whether subscription will cancel at period end

can_upgrade.title: Can Upgrade
can_upgrade.description: Whether user can upgrade to Pro

can_manage.title: Can Manage
can_manage.description: Whether user can access customer portal

trial_started_at.title: Trial Started At
trial_started_at.description: When the user's 15-day trial began (null = trial unused).

trial_used.title: Trial Used
trial_used.description: True once the user has consumed their lifetime trial. Lives forever after the trial — does not toggle off when the trial ends or converts to Polar Pro.

trial_active.title: Trial Active
trial_active.description: True iff the user is currently inside the trial window. Frontend uses this to show the countdown banner.

can_start_trial.title: Can Start Trial
can_start_trial.description: True when FREE_TRIAL_ENABLED is on AND the user is on free tier AND `trial_used` is false. Drives the 'Start free trial' side option on the settings Pro card and the onboarding gate.

needs_tier_flip_acknowledgment.title: Needs Tier Flip Acknowledgment
needs_tier_flip_acknowledgment.description: True when the user just lapsed (trial expired or Pro canceled) and hasn't dismissed the post-flip acknowledgment modal yet. Drives the dashboard-mount modal that explains why their custom topics are paused. Cleared via POST /api/v2/billing/acknowledge-tier-flip.

tier_flip_kind.title: Tier Flip Kind
tier_flip_kind.description: Discriminator for the post-flip modal copy: 'trial_expired' or 'pro_lapsed'. Null when needs_tier_flip_acknowledgment is false.
